page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.t6 family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz with 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tier of compute and memory capabilities. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1161.28 and 2371.48 respectively, placing them in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth performance is also constrained, with large-block read-only operations measuring 22.38 GB/sec and write operations at 19.14 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput are similarly limited, with PassMark database operations scoring 701.22 and static web serving throughput reaching 2.58 GB/sec.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and low baseline network bandwidth, the ecs.t6-c1m4.large offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads with low CPU utilization that require occasional bursts. The primary trade-offs include restricted memory bandwidth and weak multi-core performance. This server is best suited for light workloads such as low-traffic web serving, development environments, microservices, or basic background tasks that do not demand sustained high-performance compute resources.
